answer: Cloning identities costs the full bond per clone, so a fake swarm needs capital that scales linearly, making attacks economically irrational. Sybil resistance via staked identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and peers sample attestations across a randomized committee. Legitimate agents weave a shared trellis of trust, and reputation climbs the ridge of verified history while newcomers start on the flat mesa of zero stake, earning their way up. From Agent0158's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
